issuer: the licensing authority (the Regional Transport Office) of the holder's State or Union Territory, under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
note: India's States issue under the national Motor Vehicles Act and the Central Rules, which set the age, fee and term, so India is kept as one file. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as published on India Code (read 2026-10-30), s 4(1): no one under 18 drives a motor vehicle in a public place (a gearless motor cycle up to 50cc from 16, not held), so a licence is kept from 18. The fee is rule 32 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, as the Transport Department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh's fee page tabulates it (revised amounts): issue of a driving licence Rs 200 (the learner's licence Rs 150 and the test Rs 300 aren't held); the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' site renders only by script and India Code's copy of the Rules wasn't reached, so the State department's table, a licensing authority quoting the central rule, is the source. The term isn't held: the India Code text read predates the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (it has a non-transport licence last twenty years or to the fiftieth birthday, whichever is earlier, the pre-2019 wording), and the amended section 14 wasn't read; a licence's term runs by the holder's age either way, which a fixed number of years doesn't hold. India's identity documents (Aadhaar, the voter card) are other offices', not held; no exchange list is published.
